title: L40S: cap default concurrency + tune preemption/backpressure; document config notes
author: Lena Fischer
release_notes:
- L40S default profile now caps concurrency and tightens backpressure to reduce OOM / fragmentation under bursty traffic.
- Preemption + queue limits adjusted to prioritize decode stability over peak throughput on mixed workloads.
- Config examples updated with explicit L40S caveats + override guidance.
body:
Summary
This PR makes Redwood runtime defaults safer on L40S pools by capping default concurrency and tightening preemption/backpressure behavior. The goal is to reduce OOM/fragmentation events and p99 latency spikes observed under burst traffic and mixed prompt lengths on L40S (see SUP-21958 and recent Jan bench runs).

Motivation / context
- L40S has materially less effective memory headroom vs H100 for our current default KV-cache and mixed-workload scheduler settings.
- Under bursty traffic, the scheduler currently allows too many concurrent in-flight requests to accumulate when prefill is slow, which increases KV cache pressure and allocator fragmentation. Once fragmentation increases, we see intermittent OOMs even though steady-state memory appears under the limit.
- We want a conservative “safe default” for Hosted and for new Dedicated L40S pools, while still allowing explicit overrides (with guardrails coming in ENG-4936).

What changed
1) Default concurrency caps for L40S profile
- Introduce an explicit profile knob for L40S: max_inflight_requests (a hard cap used by admission control).
- Reduce default max_inflight_requests for L40S from “derived from GPU” to a fixed cap tuned from bench + soak results.
- Keep H100 behavior unchanged.

2) Preemption/backpressure tuning
- Adjust scheduler queue limits for L40S to avoid deep queues (which were amplifying tail latency and memory pressure).
- Reduce prefill “greediness” on L40S by tightening decode-priority thresholds when queue depth increases.
- Update backpressure to trigger earlier for long-prefill workloads (we’d rather shed/slow than thrash memory).

3) Documentation / examples
- Update profile pack config examples to include a dedicated L40S section with rationale + expected trade-offs.
- Add explicit notes about when an operator might increase concurrency (and what to monitor: OOM rate, fragmentation estimate, compaction time).

Bench results (representative)
- Workload bucket: mixed prefill (p50 ~1.5k tokens, p95 ~6k tokens) + decode heavy (200–800 tokens), concurrency 16–96.
- L40S: OOM events reduced to 0 across soak runs at recommended cap; p99 latency improved under burst due to shallower queueing; throughput down ~3–8% at saturation (expected).
- H100: no statistically significant change (defaults unchanged).

Risk / rollout notes
- Conservative defaults: may reduce peak throughput on L40S pools if customers previously relied on higher concurrency.
- Intended as a safe default. Operators can opt up after verifying memory headroom and fragmentation behavior.
- SRE: watch scheduler_queue_ms, oom_events_total, kv_compaction_ms, allocator_fragmentation_estimate, and latency p95/p99 by profile_id.

Implementation details
- The L40S cap is applied via runtime admission control so it works consistently across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
- Preemption/backpressure changes are gated on profile.sku == L40S so behavior is SKU-scoped and deterministic.

Testing
- Unit tests for profile defaults and selection.
- Added a small integration test that asserts L40S admission control rejects requests when in-flight exceeds cap (simulated).
- Ran benchmark-lab subset locally (matrix rows attached in ENG-4927).

Checklist
- [x] Benchmarked on L40S with mixed workloads
- [x] No change to H100 defaults
- [x] Updated config examples + comments
- [x] Added/updated metrics tags where needed (follow-up dashboards in observability-pack)

Screenshots / logs
- Startup log now prints L40S-specific admission cap and queue limits (example included in docs snippet; no sensitive data).

Review conversation (highlights)
- Sofia Ivanova (requested changes): “Can we avoid hard-coding a magic number without documenting how we picked it? Also want to ensure decode priority doesn’t starve prefill.”
  - Lena Fischer (author): “Added doc notes on selection (soak stability first; throughput second) and added a guard that prevents prefill starvation by enforcing a minimum prefill share when queue depth is low.”
- Omar El-Sayed: “Please confirm this won’t hide fragmentation issues; we still need signals.”
  - Lena: “Agreed—kept fragmentation estimate + compaction counters; doc explicitly calls out thresholds to watch before raising concurrency.”
- Irene Choi: “Any infra constraints? L40S fleet is mixed in a few regions.”
  - Lena: “No driver/CUDA gating here; purely runtime defaults by SKU. Compatibility gates tracked separately.”
- Sean Gallagher: “Rollout: can we add a note about rollback toggles?”
  - Lena: “Added a note pointing to the profile pack kill-switch and profile pinning guidance; no behavior change for operators who pin.”

Approvals
- Sofia Ivanova: Approved after changes
- Omar El-Sayed: Approved
- Irene Choi: Approved
- Sean Gallagher: Approved with rollout note

Merge plan
Squash merge into main; will ride runtime-1.22 train and be enabled in Hosted canary cohort first.
commits: runtime/scheduler: apply SKU-scoped queue limits + decode-priority thresholds for L40S
runtime/admission: enforce max_inflight_requests cap from active profile
profiles: set conservative L40S defaults; keep H100 unchanged
docs: update profile pack config examples with L40S guidance
tests: add coverage for L40S admission cap + default selection
